result.comment: The architecture for story-003 is ready for your review: a new `repo labels setup` command that reads all GitHub labels, adopts matches without touching them, and creates only the missing ones after your confirmation or `--yes`. Main decisions: GitHub setup stores nothing, so the connection revision cannot change. The GitHub client only gets 'list' and 'create', so rename, recolour and delete are impossible. Setup and `repo connection check` share one planner, so they always report the same. The warning uses the reader's real rules, so `Bug` or `mode: plan` warn but `Coding Agent: CLAUDE` (which the reader accepts) does not. The daemon code is not edited, which keeps K-04 and keeps story-002 on separate files. Assumed: no terminal and no `--yes` exits successfully with 'nothing written'. One GitHub promise is not in its docs page: case-only duplicates are refused; your live run confirms it. Next: your review of this architecture; acceptance criteria and tasks come in the next stage.

draft.name: Label setup command with GitHub

user_story.actor: factory owner who tracks a project on GitHub
user_story.want: to run one command that checks the project's GitHub labels, shows what it would create, and creates only the missing Mode, Coding Agent and bug labels
user_story.benefit: the factory's labels exist without me creating them by hand, existing labels stay untouched, I am warned about existing labels the factory cannot use, and running it again changes nothing
notes: Covers: O-01, O-02, O-08, O-11, O-14, O-16, O-17, O-19 (GitHub part), O-04 (GitHub part, see Ruling)

Ruling: O-04 — here the check reports missing GitHub labels and names the setup command; Linear reporting comes with the Linear setup story — Linear setup does not exist yet — cost if wrong: Linear projects get no label report until that story lands

Ruling: O-01 — the dry run and apply are delivered here for GitHub only; Linear is added by the Linear setup story — the Linear label API is not verified yet — cost if wrong: the same command is only half useful until then

Ruling: O-02 — adoption stays non-destructive, so an existing label that matches only when upper or lower case is ignored is adopted as it is, even if the factory's reader refuses that spelling; setup and the connection check then warn and name the label instead of fixing it — renaming would break the never-rename rule — cost if wrong: the owner must correct such a label by hand before the factory can use it
Size M (supplied): a new command, GitHub label read and create calls, check output and hints
Assumption: for a Linear-tracked project the command stops with a plain 'not available yet' message and changes nothing
Assumption: a Coding Agent label is wanted for each runner the factory registers today (Claude and Codex), read when the command runs
Assumption: label colours and short descriptions are the factory's choice, one colour per family (Mode, Coding Agent, bug)
Assumption: the bug label is matched by the name bug, ignoring upper or lower case
Assumption: the reader's rules for which names it accepts are the ones in force today and stay unchanged (K-04); the warning uses those same rules
Assumption: GitHub proof is tests with a fake GitHub plus one live dry run and apply by the owner on a test repository

draft.problem: A GitHub-tracked project only works with the factory's Mode, Coding Agent and bug labels, and today the owner must create each one by hand. Nothing tells the owner which ones are missing or where to fix it. The owner needs a safe way to see what is there, see what would be created, and approve it. The command must never rename, recolour, delete or duplicate a label that already exists. Because an existing label can match by name and still be refused by the factory's reader, the owner also needs to be told when that happens instead of being told setup succeeded.
in_scope: New command `litefactory repo labels setup <project>` that picks the tracker the project uses for tickets (O-11)
Dry run first: lists labels found, labels it would create (O-01)
Applies after confirmation, or at once with --yes; with no terminal and no --yes it shows the dry run and writes nothing, not one GitHub write (O-01, O-14)
GitHub: ensures Mode: Research, Plan, Implement, Validate, Spike; Coding Agent: one per registered runner; and bug (O-02)

Existing labels are matched by exact name, ignoring upper or lower case, and adopted as they are; an adopted label keeps its exact spelling, colour and description, and no second label is created for it (O-02)
Only missing labels are created, with a consistent colour and short description per family (O-02)
Label discovery reads every page of the project's labels, so a label beyond the first page is found and not created again (O-02, O-17)

Adopted warning: when an adopted label's name is one the factory's reader refuses, setup reports it as a warning naming the label and the reason, and the connection check shows the same warning; the label is never renamed or recreated (O-02, O-04, see Ruling)
Running it twice changes nothing; a run with nothing to create says so, makes zero GitHub writes and writes no new connection revision (O-01, O-17)

If a create fails, the command stops, reports what was created and what failed, and stores nothing, so the connection revision is unchanged; a rerun adopts what was created and creates only what is still missing (O-16)
`repo connection check` reports missing GitHub labels as a warning and names the setup command, and never changes the connection revision (O-04, GitHub part)
`repo add` and `repo connection set` print a one-line hint naming the setup command, and do not run it (O-08)

Tests with a fake GitHub cover: adopted labels the reader refuses, a label list longer than one page, case-different existing labels left unchanged, nothing missing with zero writes, a non-terminal run without --yes with zero writes, a failed create with unchanged connection revision, a rerun after a partial failure, and a no-op run with unchanged connection revision; plus one live dry run and apply by the owner on a test repository (O-19)
not_in_scope: N-01 — No deleting, renaming or recolouring of any label, including old grey auto-created ones such as lisisite's `Mode: Research`.
N-02 — No moving existing flat Linear labels into groups.
N-03 — No labels beyond Mode, Coding Agent and bug (no priority, type or status labels).
N-04 — No removal of a Coding Agent label when a runner is no longer registered.
N-05 — No creating Linear labels at workspace level.
N-07 — No background or scheduled label sync; setup runs on request only.

K-01 — Never rename, recolour, delete or duplicate existing labels, and never touch labels the factory does not own. Existing cockpit (MAR) connections and flat names such as `Mode: Plan` keep working unchanged.
K-03 — A connection without the new maps behaves exactly as today, and manual `--mode-labels` editing stays supported.
K-04 — GitHub mode and agent label names and how the daemon reads them stay unchanged.
Not here: Linear label setup, grouped Linear labels and storing Linear label IDs (later stories)

general.decision: A new command; nothing is retired. Hand-made labels and manual `--mode-labels` editing keep working. Behaviour is proven with a fake GitHub; the one live dry run and apply on a test repository is an owner check, not an automated test.
general.rationale: Feature mode adds without superseding; integration mode says live-only proof is an owner action (O-19).

general.decision: `litefactory repo labels setup <project-id> [--yes]`, using the numeric project ID like the `repo connection` commands. It reads the project's current ticket connection. GitHub: runs. Linear: stops with a plain 'not available yet' precondition message, no network call, nothing written. No ticket connection or a disabled one: precondition refusal naming `repo connection set`.
general.rationale: The ticket connection already says which tracker a project uses; one ID style across `repo` commands avoids a second lookup rule.

general.decision: One pure function builds the wanted list: the five Mode labels from the existing canonical mode label names (`Mode: Research` … `Mode: Spike`), one `Coding Agent: <Name>` for each agent enabled in the factory config at run time (today Claude and Codex), and `bug`. No agent binary is started. Fixed colour per family (Mode, Coding Agent, bug) and a short description under 100 characters. The order is fixed, so output and creates are repeatable.
general.rationale: Reusing the canonical names keeps K-04. Reading the config matches the daemon's runner registry, which is built from the same config sections.

general.decision: A new GitHub client call lists every repository label through the existing page walker (100 per page, existing 100-page safety bound). Planning starts only after the full list is read. A failed page or a hit bound stops the run with zero writes; the command never plans from a partial list.
general.rationale: A partial list would make a label on a later page look missing and get created again.

general.decision: A wanted label matches an existing one when the full names are equal ignoring upper or lower case. A match is adopted as it is. The GitHub client gains only list and create; there is no update or delete call, so rename, recolour and delete cannot happen. Labels the factory does not want are ignored.
general.rationale: Leaving out edit calls makes the never-touch rule hold by construction, not by care.

general.decision: Each adopted name is checked against today's reader rules: a mode label must equal its canonical name byte for byte; a Coding Agent label must start with exactly `Coding Agent: ` and its value must have the agent-name shape (capital first letter) and name that runner; the bug label must be exactly `bug` (the daemon's bug routing compares exactly). So `mode: plan`, `coding agent: Claude` and `Bug` warn; `Coding Agent: CLAUDE` is accepted by the reader and does not warn. The rules live in a new pure helper in the agent package. Daemon reading code is not edited; a new daemon-package test runs one sample table through the daemon's resolvers and the helper and fails if they disagree.
general.rationale: A plain spelling compare would warn wrongly about names the reader accepts. Not touching the daemon keeps K-04 and keeps story-002's area free.

general.decision: The dry run is always printed first: labels found (exact spelling), labels to create, warnings. Nothing to create: says so, no prompt, zero writes. `--yes`: apply at once. Terminal on input: ask y/N; anything but y or yes writes nothing. No terminal and no `--yes`: print the dry run and 'nothing written, rerun with --yes', exit 0. The CLI environment gains an 'input is a terminal' fact set by the entry point, so tests can control it.
general.rationale: Writes need either a person at the prompt or an explicit flag. Exit 0 because nothing failed; this is an assumption the acceptance stage may tighten.

general.decision: Creates run one at a time in the fixed order. The first failure stops the run. The report lists created labels, the failed one with a plain reason (for example 'no write access to issues'), and the ones not tried. A create is never retried inside one run. A rerun reads the labels again, adopts what was created and creates only what is still missing.
general.rationale: A rerun from a fresh read is the simplest safe recovery and needs no stored progress.

general.decision: GitHub setup stores nothing: it writes no connection version, no observation and no other store row. The connection revision therefore stays unchanged on every path (success, no-op, refusal, failure) by construction. Story-001's Linear label fields are not touched.
general.rationale: GitHub labels are found by name, so there is no ID to keep. Tests can still assert the revision is unchanged.

general.decision: Relied on: list repository labels is page-number paginated with at most 100 per page; create takes name, colour as six hex digits without `#`, and description up to 100 characters, and answers 201 or 422 on validation failure (GitHub REST docs). Relied on but not stated on that page: GitHub refuses a second label whose name differs only in case. Our case-insensitive match means we never try that; if GitHub ever accepted it we would still not duplicate, because we only create names not found. The live owner run confirms behaviour. Create needs write access to the repository's issues (fine-grained token: Issues write); a 403 goes down the failure path. Create is not idempotent: on a lost reply the run stops and a rerun adopts the label. At most 8 sequential writes per run, far under rate limits; a rate-limit reply is a normal failure.
general.rationale: These are the only provider promises the story needs; each has a limit and a fallback recorded here, not left for Implement.

general.decision: For an enabled GitHub ticket-role connection, after today's checks pass, the check makes one more paginated label read and runs the same planner as setup. It appends to the remedy: missing labels with the setup command, and each reader warning with the label and reason. Status, reason and capabilities values stay as today. A failed label read adds 'labels could not be read' and changes nothing else. The CLI passes the configured agent names into the check; a caller that does not pass them skips only the Coding Agent comparison. Code-role and Linear connections are unchanged. The check keeps saving only its observation, never a new connection revision.
general.rationale: One planner makes setup and check agree. Stable status values protect other consumers, the same rule story-001 used.

general.decision: `repo add` prints one line after registering: run `litefactory repo labels setup <id>` to create the factory's labels. No network call. `repo connection set` prints the same line after a successful save. Neither runs setup.
general.rationale: The hint is fixed text; `repo add` stays offline.

general.decision: Shared edits: the CLI command list (story-004 extends the same command), `repo connection` CLI file (story-001 adds flags; dependency exists), the connection check (story-001 edits the Linear part, story-004 adds Linear label reporting and depends on this story), and `repo add`. This story adds a new file in the agent package and does not edit the Linear reader or daemon agent code, which story-002 changes. So story-002 and story-003 do not overlap, and no set revision is needed.
general.rationale: Merge conflicts happen only between stories with no dependency; the only independent sibling (story-002) is kept on separate files.

general.decision: No agent markdown or skill changes and no agent instruction prose in Go; command output is owner-facing CLI text. Tests check behaviour (planner, client calls against a fake GitHub, CLI flow, check remedy built by code), never shipped markdown wording.
general.rationale: These are the agent-guidance and testing standards that apply to this role.

service_design.responsibility: Parse project ID and `--yes`, print the dry run, ask for confirmation when input is a terminal, print the result. Prints hints in `repo add` and `repo connection set`.
service_design.access: Calls the local projects service only; never calls GitHub directly. Reads the agent list from loaded config.

service_design.responsibility: Load the current ticket connection, gate on provider, get GitHub clients through the existing connection factory (same credential and actor checks as the connection check), build the plan, then apply it on request.
service_design.access: Read-only store access. Network only through the connection factory's GitHub client.

service_design.responsibility: List all repository labels; create one label.
service_design.access: REST through the existing request wrapper and page walker. No update or delete calls.

service_design.responsibility: Add the label read and the planner's missing and warning lines to the remedy.
service_design.access: Same client and timeout as today's check; saves only its observation.

solution_design.contract: Input: wanted labels, all discovered labels. Output: adopted (wanted name, existing exact name), to create (in fixed order), warnings (label, reason). No I/O.
solution_design.rationale: Setup and check share it, so they always agree and it is easy to test.

solution_design.contract: Given a family and an existing label name, says whether today's reader accepts it and, if not, why. Mirrors today's mode, Coding Agent and bug rules; a daemon-package test proves it agrees with the daemon resolvers.
solution_design.rationale: Gives the warning the reader's real rules without editing the daemon (K-04).

solution_design.contract: Lists created, failed (one, with reason) and not tried. Empty created and failed means nothing was written.
solution_design.rationale: Lets the CLI print O-16's report and tests assert write counts.
